title: Pauri 13: trusting, awareness
hook: mannai: by trust the mind becomes aware and knows all realms (Japji 13)
tomorrow: Pauri 14: trusting, the path is clear

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pauri 12: the one who trusts can't be described. Your line was no pen for this. Did something stay bigger than your words? Today, what trusting does to the mind. Day one hundred eighty-four.

You'd think trust would make you sleepy. Relax, you've got this, lean back. But watch a child on a parent's shoulders at a parade. Because she's safe up there, she sees everything: the drummers, the balloons, the dog in the crowd. The child on the ground, gripping a hand and worried about getting lost, sees knees. Safety doesn't dull her. It frees her attention to look around. Pauri 13 makes a claim like that. Trusting doesn't put the mind to sleep. It wakes it up.
screen: `A CHILD ON A PARENT'S SHOULDERS.` → `SAFE, SO SHE SEES EVERYTHING.` → `TRUST WAKES THE MIND.`

segments.voice: Pauri 13 opens: mannai surat hovai man budh. By trusting, surat comes into the mind and the understanding. Surat is today's word, and it's one of the great words of Sikh teaching. It means awareness, attention, consciousness, the part of you that is awake and noticing. In Sikh thought, surat is what attunes to the shabad, the Word, the way a radio tunes to a station. The Gurus speak of surat joined to shabad as the heart of the path. Then the pauri goes on, in paraphrase. By trusting, one knows of all the realms, every world. By trusting, one doesn't take blows to the face. By trusting, one doesn't go off with the messenger of death. And the refrain: such is the Name of the Stainless One, known only to the one who trusts it in the mind. Notice the order. Awareness comes first. Before knowing all realms, before escaping fear, the first gift of trust is that you wake up. That fits what we've heard. Listening gave direction; trusting gives attention. And it fits an ordinary Tuesday. When you're anxious, your attention shrinks to one tight spot, the worry. When you trust, it opens. You notice the light on the wall, the tone in someone's voice, what the moment is actually asking. The blows to the face and the messenger of death are the stanza's picture of fear itself. A mind that trusts doesn't flinch at every shadow. It has room to see.
screen: `MANNAI SURAT HOVAI MAN BUDH.` · `SURAT — AWARENESS, ATTENTION.` · `AWARENESS COMES FIRST.` · `FEAR SHRINKS, TRUST OPENS.` · then, large: `TRUST WAKES YOU.`

segments.voice: Be aware of your whole body, once. Start at the top of your head and let attention move down slowly: face, jaw, shoulders, arms, hands, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. Don't fix anything. Just notice. When you reach your feet, try to feel the whole body at once, one shape, breathing. Rest there. If the mind narrows onto a worry, widen it again to the whole body. The bell holds the time.
Surat. Awareness, attention, the waking consciousness that tunes to the Word. By trusting, Pauri 13 says, surat comes.
Your line: trust wakes you. Today, when you feel safe for a moment, don't just relax: look around, and notice three things you'd normally miss. Day one hundred eighty-four.

screen: `DAY 184 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: PAURI 14: TRUSTING, THE PATH IS CLEAR.`

howItsDone: Pauri 13 is part of the morning Japji; many Sikhs speak of surat, awareness, being joined to the shabad as the center of their practice, especially while listening to kirtan or reciting the Name.

myth: in Pauri 13, trusting makes the mind dull and sleepy
the first gift it names is surat: awareness comes into the mind.
surat is a key word in Sikh teaching about the Word
surat joined to shabad, awareness tuned to the Word, is at the heart of the path.
Pauri 13 ends with the same refrain as Pauri 12
such is the Name of the Stainless One, known to the one who trusts.

fork.setup: you trust, fully. according to Pauri 13, what's the first thing that happens?
fork.reveal: mannai surat hovai man budh: by trusting, awareness comes into the mind and understanding, and only then the knowing of all realms.

original.note: Gurmukhi: surat, awareness or attentive consciousness; in Sikh teaching, what attunes to the shabad.

trapdoor: what you thought: trusting means switching off.
what it means: trusting frees the mind to wake up and pay attention.
what a scholar hears: surat, attentive consciousness, is paired with shabad across Sikh scripture; here it's the first fruit of mannai.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 3 (Japji, Pauri 13, line 1)

notes: Pauri 13 paraphrased; 'blows to the face' and 'messenger of death' (jam) glossed as the stanza's pictures of fear. Some commentators read these as punishment at death; confirm the Keeper's preferred framing.
Surat-shabad as the heart of the path: common Sikh teaching (e.g., Siddh Gosht), stated generally without a specific citation; confirm.
Ang number and pronunciation SUR-at; confirm.
